title: Get fast proof of Intent scope timing history

intentCoverage.report:
Verdict: Assertion gap.

Story and revision: SEED-413#speed-intent-scope-timing-history (plan 774), revision 112ade7728073765cc253f79c275f852841f9431. Promise: entry, folder, file and revision keys keep distinct kept histories across remounts. A late reply for an old endpoint revision cannot replace or erase the newer key's shown history.

Fault: in dashboard/src/useIntentCiEndpointHistory.ts, success branch line 64, `if (!controller.signal.aborted) {` became `if (true) {`. A late answer for an aborted older read is now applied. Fixtures and assertions were unchanged.

Maintained assertion examined: dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-project-scope-history-key-isolation.spec.ts:56-58: `old.resolve(...)`, `await old.ask()`, `await expect.poll(() => history.readout().selected).toBe(shown)`. With the fault in place it PASSED (1 test passed, 461 ms). Its reach: the poll runs after the old reply resolves on the intended path. But it passes on its first sample, before React commits the late setReading.

Independent witness: a throwaway copy of the spec in the scratch checkout only (zz-scratch-witness.spec.ts). It inserted a 300 ms wait and a readout log after `await old.ask()`. With the fault it logged `WITNESS selected after late old reply: {}`. The same poll then failed with "expected undefined to be 'Observed trunk endpoint b2b2b2b · 11.…'". The late old-key answer overwrote the hook state, the key filter at line 107 then hid everything, and the newer revision's shown history disappeared. This is wrong behavior on the exact path the maintained assertion checks. The maintained assertion did not observe it.

Commands, run in a detached scratch worktree at the revision after `npm ci`:
`caffeinate -s -i env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run --silent test:dashboard:frontend -- --workers 2 dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-project-scope-history-key-isolation.spec.ts`. The witness spec was run with the same command and its own path.
- Baseline: 1 passed (720 ms test, 2.87 s run).
- Faulted: maintained 1 passed; witness 1 failed (wrong behavior observed).
- Restored: the fault was reverted with git checkout through an EXIT trap and the witness file was deleted. `git diff --quiet` was clean, HEAD was unchanged, and the same command gave 1 passed (583 ms). The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force`.

Next proof action: strengthen the observing assertion so it cannot pass before React commits the late answer. For example, flush or settle the render after `await old.ask()` (an act/flush, or a wait for a commit signal) before checking that `selected` still equals `shown`. A single `expect.poll` first-sample pass is not evidence.

Costs: test runtime about 9.8 s of runner time (baseline 2.87 s, faulted 1.85 s, witness 2.99 s, restored 2.05 s); human and agent effort unavailable; invocation-to-report elapsed 75310 ms (measured).

Wrap-up disposition (checked revision 112ade772): assertion gap on the delivered key-isolation late-answer check; no delivered product defect (the wrong behavior appears only under the scratch fault). The outcome fits the existing follow-up: plan 777's "Correction of the delivered scope timing history entry" already owns strengthening this assertion (force a commit after the late answer, break-check the abort guard and key filter); its first bullet now links this evidence. One queue entry: SEED-413#speed-intent-scope-timing-reading stays first in the Backlog list.
